environment.label: FUNCTIONAL SCALE on an 8-logical-CPU / 32 GB Windows 11 dev machine, database co-located in Docker on the same host. NOT the reference scale of R22.

design.wf2JoinStorm: 100 WF-2 instances; both comment branches completed at the same instant (barrier per pair)
design.threadsPerVariant: one-root scenarios run once with 16 and once with 32 threads
design.classification: PG 40P01 deadlock / 40001 serialization / 55P03 lock timeout; Oracle ORA-00060 deadlock / ORA-08177 / ORA-30006,00054; SQL Server 1205 deadlock / 3960 / 1222; engine *OptimisticLockingException = OLE
design.pass: 0 lost updates and 0 unrecovered failures after retries (raw OLE/deadlock counts are reported, not judged)
design.historyLevel: as configured by the adapters: Flowable engine default (audit), Operaton FULL (set by the adapter)
design.oneRootUserTasks: 6 roots x 50 parallel user tasks (fork/join), completed concurrently
design.oneRootMessages: 10 roots x 32 parallel message catch events (fork/join), correlated concurrently
design.retry: max 5 retries, exponential back-off with full jitter, base 20 ms, cap 1 s (VI.1.1 rule 7)
design.lostUpdateCheck: after the concurrent phase: every variable written by a command that reported success must be present; then commands that failed after their retries are re-run sequentially (drain, not counted as successes) so the instance can finish, and the join must have fired exactly once and the instance ended exactly once (runtime, ACT_HI_PROCINST, ACT_HI_ACTINST)

notes: Host contention: two or more other agents ran PostgreSQL/SQL Server containers and builds on the same machine during every run; machine CPU averaged 88-100% (JVM view) during the E9 steady windows. All E6/E9 runs here finished BEFORE the shared heavy-build lock rule was announced (about 14:45 local), so they overlapped other lanes; 0 minutes were spent waiting for the lock.

Test-harness workarounds (not adapter or engine changes): (1) product-api LeaseTable SQL rewritten by a JDBC proxy on Oracle (BIGINT -> NUMBER(19)) and SQL Server (IF NOT EXISTS, FOR UPDATE); without it neither adapter can be constructed on those DBs. (2) Flowable message correlation in E6 goes through RuntimeService because EngineAdapter.correlateMessage (Flowable) finds no execution for a catch event inside a parallel branch. (3) E9 starts Flowable's async executor and sets the history level on the built engine.
Runs: PostgreSQL 13:24-13:30, Oracle Free 14:21-14:36, SQL Server 14:37-14:55 (2026-11-04, local time), one container at a time.
